recentItems.title: SA defends Palestinian rights ahead of UN debate
recentItems.description:
Defence of international law and Palestinian rights has taken centre stage in New York. South Africa's International Relations Minister Ronald Lamola joined U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders, UNAIDS Executive Director Winnie Byanyima and Palestinian-American organiser Aber Kawas at the "We Shall Not Be Moved" gathering.

The event was organised in collaboration with The Hague Group to affirm that the UN Charter recognises the growing challenges to the international legal order. 

Sanders introduced Lamola to the gathering, as South Africa again positioned itself at the forefront of calls for accountability over Gaza and for international law to be applied without double standards.

recentItems.title: Young unemployed people in Malelane demand jobs
recentItems.description:
Young people of Nkomazi local Municipality have handed over a memorandum of grievances to the Kruger National Park in Malelane, Mpumalanga.

They are demanding job and business opportunities, and say they have been applying for years with no response. 

SABC News Reporter Nhlanhla Jele spoke to them.

recentItems.title: Strong winds leave Tafelsig homes damaged
recentItems.description:
Residents in Maanskynkop Road in Tafelsig, Mitchells Plain say they are shell-shocked after strong winds ripped off the roofs of their homes. 

Authorities say about 50 structures have been affected.

 Residents report experiencing hail, rain, thunder and lightning at around 4 am. 

SABC News reporter Vanessa Poonah has more.

recentItems.title: Over 100 people working at Alberton steel company illegally: Sibiya
recentItems.description:
Employment and Labour Deputy Minister Jomo Sibiya, his Home Affairs counterpart Njabulo Nzuza and Ekurhuleni Mayor Nkosindiphile Xhakaza are leading a labour and immigration raid in Alberton, East Rand.

They are raiding companies to monitor compliance with immigration laws, labour laws and bylaws. 

SABC News reporter Mbalenhle Mthethwa interviewed Sibiya.

recentItems.title: SAPS Arrest | Sexual offences case of top police official delayed
recentItems.description:
A high-ranking police official is expected to appear in the Randburg Magistrates’ Court in Johannesburg on Tuesday.

The Commission's Recommendations Task Team arrested the Lieutenant-General on Monday.

The official is facing charges related to sexual offences after allegedly sexually grooming of a 16-year-old girl between July and August this year.

He is also accused of raping an 18-year-old woman at a hotel in Sandton in May 2026.

SABC News anchor Heidi Giokos has the details

recentItems.title: In conversation with US Ambassador to SA Leo Brent Bozell III
recentItems.description:
The US ambassador to South Africa, Leo Brent Bozell says America will not release the names of South Africans affected by the visa restrictions. 

The US State Department made an announcement that visa restrictions will be imposed on government officials and other South Africans who have played a role in the land expropriation law, and those who are continuing to promote the "kill the boer, kill the farmer" song.

Speaking to SABC News Specialist correspondent, Sophie Mokoena, Bozell touched on a range of issues.

recentItems.title: Brown Mogotsi denied bail for fourth time
recentItems.description:
North West businessman Brown Mogotsi has been denied bail in his fourth application by the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court. 

The court found that the addresses presented by Mogotsi were not new facts, as they had already been considered in his previous bail applications. 

SABC News' Chriselda Lewis reports.

recentItems.title: SIU conducts raid on PSIRA head office in Centurion
recentItems.description:
The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) is currently raiding the Private Security Industry Regulatory Authority (PSIRA) head office in Centurion. 

This is in connection with an investigation regarding a R 30 million contract.

 PSIRA was meant to provide three services including end-to-end user training, grade C and E security training and election observer training for over 7000 people across all provinces, in partnership with the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF). 

SABC News reporter Lopang Alamu is covering the raid.
